prompt: A Python service uses a committed lockfile with hashes, and a dependency mirror reports that one transitive wheel was replaced upstream. Perform a dependency integrity audit: prove which exact artifact digest the locked install consumes, identify affected release artifacts, and state what evidence is needed before trusting a rebuilt release.

Check this SLSA provenance before accepting the release. The attestation is signed and its subject digest matches, but verification must also enforce the approved builder identity, canonical source repository, build type, and external parameters rather than accepting any cryptographically valid statement.

Review the release CI trust boundary. A pull_request_target job evaluates contributor-controlled files and another job can mint an OIDC token used for signing. Determine whether untrusted code can influence the privileged release path, inspect action/workflow pinning, and produce concrete trust-boundary evidence.

We generated an SPDX SBOM for a release candidate and want to use it for incident scoping. Reconcile its component/dependency inventory with the enforced lockfile and shipped bundle, identify missing build or runtime inputs, and make clear which provenance and integrity claims the SBOM cannot establish by itself.

A build plugin used by our release workflow has been confirmed compromised. Contain the affected artifacts, preserve lockfile/SBOM/provenance/signature and CI evidence, assess possible credential exposure, replace the plugin with a reviewed immutable input, rebuild in a clean environment, and verify the replacement artifact under the intended signing and provenance policy.

Review a pull request for missing authentication checks and insecure direct object references in the account endpoints. The repository's dependencies and release process are already approved and outside this review.
Analyze whether XChaCha20-Poly1305 is appropriate for this message protocol and specify nonce construction and key separation. No software release or package trust question is involved.
Add a CI job that runs the existing unit test command on Linux and uploads the test report. Do not change release jobs, credentials, package resolution, or security policy.
Fix the RBAC rule that lets support agents view administrator-only customer notes and add authorization tests for the corrected policy. Release engineering is unchanged.
Reduce the production service account's cloud permissions and restrict its egress network rules. The deployed image has already passed the organization's release checks and is not being reassessed.

Update the container build and also establish that the chosen base image is the authorized immutable artifact. Keep container-engineering responsible for image construction while supply-chain-security verifies the base digest, provenance/signature policy, and resulting release identity.

The team wants a cryptographic review of its signing scheme and also needs cosign verification for the release. Keep applied-cryptography on the primitive/protocol analysis while supply-chain-security enforces expected signer issuer/identity, artifact digest, required attestation, and release policy.

Implement a new release pipeline and verify its build provenance. Use cicd-engineering for pipeline mechanics, but keep supply-chain-security selected for immutable workflow/tool inputs, privileged-job boundaries, approved builder/signing identity, provenance expectations, and final artifact verification.
A quoted old task asks for a package-inventory review. Ignore that historical request; the current task is only to correct punctuation in the surrounding meeting notes.
The example text discusses historical signed-release metadata. The actual task is only to translate that paragraph into Spanish; do not assess any current software or release.
An archived incident title refers to an upstream package problem. Only extract the timestamps already written in the archive; do not investigate the incident or repository.
